subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm thinking about whether this vehicle needs a full joint hierarchy, deciding to add a modest rig with hull, turret, barrel, wheels, and stabilizer legs so parts can attach to bones without overcomplicating things.

Now I'm planning the overall layout: an 11m long, 3m wide, 3.2m tall chassis with six wheels and a forward-pointing railgun turret mounted over the cab, plus four hydraulic outrigger legs for stabilization. I'm working out specific coordinates for wheel placement, axle spacing, and leg deployment points relative to the ground plane, using decal textures and emissive glow accents for surface detail.

I'm sketching the frame hierarchy — chassis box, frustumBox lower hull, sloped-windshield cab, turret ring joint, and a dual-rail railgun cradle with a breech block and glowing capacitor cylinders on the rear deck. I'm deciding to keep the barrel mostly horizontal with a slight upward tilt rather than relying on joint rotation, simplifying the aim direction for the trunnion pivot.

Now I'm defining the joint hierarchy — hull root, turret pivoting up from the hull, gun mounted on the turret aiming forward along Z — plus wheel axle joints and leg/piston joints for suspension, each with explicit positions and directions. I'm working out the wheel assembly next: tire and hub cylinders sized and colored, with a ring of small lug-nut cylinders computed at specific model-space positions around the hub.

I'm deciding to skip torus tread detailing and instead paint a tread pattern directly as texture grain on the tire cylinder, and opting for simple box-shaped mudguard slabs above each wheel rather than curved half-cylinder fenders to avoid backface shading issues. I'm sketching out a short list of textures to generate, starting with a chevron warning stripe and a unit emblem roundel.

I'm planning a digital camo paint scheme using patches of three green tones over an olive base with countershading, plus glow accents for the cab windows, capacitor cores, and rail strips. For the four stabilizer legs, I'm working out mounts on the hull sides connected by diagonal struts to pads on the ground, using direct rod connections from mount to pad.

Now I'm refining the legs into a telescoping design with a thicker outer sleeve and thinner inner piston, plus bracing struts and a hydraulic cylinder, ball-joint pads, and treating each leg as a bone-driven joint. I'm also planning a round of hull detailing: skirts, armor panels, rear vents, ammo boxes, antennas, a radar dish, searchlight, smoke launchers, tow hooks, glowing headlights, exhaust stacks, a ladder, stowage boxes, a roof hatch, mirrors, and bumpers.

Now I'm designing the railgun itself -- breech, rails, muzzle brake with coil rings, insulator cylinders, glowing central channel, cradle plates, and rear capacitor banks, while figuring out the turret body shape using a chamfered box or lathe-based cylinder geometry.

Checking the clearances now: turret base sits at hull top around y 2.4, trunnion supports rise to y 3.9, and the gun axis at y 3.6 needs to clear the cab roof at y 3.1, so the barrel passes safely over the cab.

Overall length spans from -5.2 to 9, roughly 14m, with height near 3.9 -- a sizeable vehicle. I'm setting up a helper box function for construction and defining the color palette (olive, tan, gun metal, steel, black, yellow, cyan, red) along with camo patch logic for painting the hull.

Adding dirt and shading logic...

I also need to check which helper functions are importable from the SDK, and plan decal planes on the hull sides using textured geometry aimed outward with default world-up orientation.

For the textures I'm planning out a set: an emblem roundel, a stencil reading "RG-6 ASTRAEUS," hazard chevron stripes, a cab glass screen with sky gradient, a warning panel, a capacitor band, and front grille vents -- roughly six decal textures total. Now I'm starting to write the actual code.

Setting up box and cylinder helper functions...

Still working out the cabin geometry...

I'm computing the windshield normal and placing it as an angled plane with the screen texture and a slight glow, then adding matching side window planes. Next I'm extending the chassis forward with a nose box and front bumper, including a chevron decal on the bumper face.

Now I'm building the hull body behind the cab as a sloped box with side skirts and stowage racks, sizing its length and center position so the turret sits correctly on top, and adding a grille-textured vent plane on the engine deck oriented with the right up-axis.

Working through wheel placement along the z-axis, I'm adjusting their x-offset to avoid overlapping the hull width, adding axle rods connecting each pair, and sizing fender boxes to sit over each wheel.

Now I'm figuring out leg mount positions along the hull sides and matching them to ground pads sized to clear the wheels, planning a simple sleeve-shaped leg connecting mount to pad.

Checking spacing between legs and wheels to make sure everything clears properly, then working out pad dimensions so the lowest point sits right at ground level with wheels touching down too.

Now I'm laying out the railgun: adding a gun joint on the turret, then building the barrel as two long rail boxes with cyan glow strips along their inner faces, plus steel spacer boxes connecting the rails at intervals along the length.

I'm adding top and bottom strap clamps across the rails, then placing glowing coil rings (torus shapes) at intervals around the barrel. For the muzzle I'm using simple top/bottom plates, and now I'm starting the breech block as a wider box section.

Next I'm positioning cradle side plates and trunnion supports beneath the turret, and planning capacitor bank cylinders mounted in rows on the rear deck behind the turret.

Now I'm shaping the turret itself as an octagonal cylinder with a darker top plate and skirt ring, adding a commander's cupola hatch with a glowing periscope, and planning a radar dish mounted on a mast at the turret's rear-left using a sphere-section geometry.

Simplifying the dish into a flat cone shape for cleaner results, then adding smoke launcher tubes angled forward-out on each side of the turret front, plus thin antenna rods.

Now placing hull decals: a roundel emblem on each side at the hull's x-extent, and a stencil text panel reading "RG-6 / ASTRAEUS" positioned to avoid clashing with the wheel fenders and leg arms, checking height and z-depth ranges so nothing overlaps.

I'm also sketching small tool-box details near the hull sides, repositioning them to clear the wheel and decal zones, and starting to block out an underside chassis panel.

For the chassis itself, I'm checking the vertical overlap with the hull body and wheels, tightening the gap so the chassis sits just below the hull without clipping. Then I'm shifting focus to the front cab, planning to extrude its profile outline from the chassis top up through the windshield area.

Working out the front nose details next: positioning headlights and grille on the cab's front face, sizing a bumper box ahead of the chassis, and adding a chevron decal across the bumper plane as a surface detail.

Now I'm adding exhaust stacks as thin vertical cylinders behind the cab, applying camo paint consistently across the hull, cab, and turret parts, and planning a small decal helper function for placing textured planes with proper orientation.

For the textures, I'm sketching several SVGs: an emblem with a ring, star, and bar; a stencil text marking; a chevron stripe pattern; a grille with dark slats; a bluish gradient screen with a diagonal glint; and a warning triangle with a bolt symbol, totaling six textures. I'm also setting up a glow helper that clones materials and applies emissive maps for the textured screen at reduced strength, then moving into writing the wheel placement loops efficiently.

Writing wheel and leg joint code...

Still placing leg components...
